headline: High: OpenMetadata’s MCP/API/webhook surface can amplify content-writing outputs into data-governance actions, while the pair also creates medium prompt-injection and leakage risks via shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing source with broad network egress; Agent B exposes MCP tools, APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. That creates a plausible path where A-generated or imported content is consumed by B as trusted input. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Agent B ingests content from Agent A via MCP, API, webhook, or event payloads without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Agent A can emit attacker-controlled text into a shared channel that B parses as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text.
Require provenance labels on all A-to-B content.
Add a fixed allowlist for B tool commands.
Review one sample A output before enabling B automation.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and provenance tracking.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B touches governance, lineage, memory, and other metadata classes and can call APIs/webhooks; Agent A has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or exchange files, B may transmit sensitive metadata outward. No shared filesystem is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty keeps it at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share files, prompts, or exported artifacts, B can ingest and forward metadata.
IF B is configured to send catalog or lineage data to external services, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Turn off any B export or sync jobs.
Inspect one outbound B request for sensitive fields.
Restrict A to non-sensitive inputs only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field redaction before any API/webhook call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B supports multiple instances and uses MCP/API/webhook tooling, while Agent A has no write or filesystem capability shown. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable resources, so direct write conflict is not evidenced. Because B’s mutable surfaces are broad but A’s are absent, the conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API or webhook target, concurrent updates can collide.
IF an orchestrator maps A’s outputs into B’s writable metadata objects, conflicts can appear.
mitigations: Assign separate targets for A and B.
Serialize any shared API writes.
Check whether B already has a lock or queue.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same dataset.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control on shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing source and Agent B is a data-engineering/catalog agent with MCP/API/webhook actions. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into metadata, lineage, or governance records. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium and note the uncertainty.
conditions: IF B uses A’s text as source-of-truth without verification, downstream records can be wrong.
IF B auto-publishes or syncs A-derived facts into catalog entries, the error propagates.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing A-derived facts.
Compare A outputs against a second source.
Mark A content as untrusted by default.
Limit B to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before B writes records.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B touches governance, lineage, memory, and tribal knowledge, which can include regulated or policy-bound data; Agent A has broad network egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot prove a breach, but the combination creates a plausible compliance mismatch if sensitive metadata flows from B to A or external services.
conditions: IF B stores EU PII, PHI, or retention-bound metadata and A receives it, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF B exports governed data to external APIs without a DPA or residency controls, the mismatch materializes.
mitigations: Classify the data before any transfer.
Block regulated fields from A inputs.
Confirm residency and retention settings in B.
Disable external sync for governed datasets.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
